chief_complaint: Management of hypertension and associated cardiometabolic risk factors (obesity, prediabetes) with attention to knee osteoarthritis pain and social housing instability.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 60‑year‑old man with a long‑standing history of essential hypertension (diagnosed 2000) currently treated with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. He has obesity (BMI ≥30) documented since 2007, prediabetes (A1c 5.9%) since 2014, and chronic knee osteoarthritis causing pain managed with naproxen. Anemia has been present since 2014 without recent laboratory characterization. Blood pressure at the most recent visit was 132/89 mmHg (stage 1 hypertension) with a resting heart rate of 97 bpm. He reports full‑time employment and has a history of unstable housing. Preventive labs (lipid panel, renal function, BMI) are missing from the record. He attends regular wellness visits but there are gaps in risk‑factor monitoring and preventive medication (no statin).
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior gingivitis and dental caries (treated 2019‑2020), a wrist sprain (resolved 2018), past part‑time employment, prior medication review entries, a history of environmental violence that has resolved, and a period of not being in the labor force (resolved 2017). The patient also has a remote surgical history of appendectomy (1997).

active_medications.name: diphenhydramine Hydrochloride 25 MG Oral Tablet
active_medications.purpose: Presumed treatment for insomnia or allergic symptoms (unspecified)

social_determinants: Housing is reported as unsatisfactory, which may affect medication adherence and lifestyle. The patient is employed full‑time and has attained higher education, suggesting stable income and health literacy but limited time for health‑promoting activities.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 1 hypertension (132/89 mmHg), elevated resting heart rate (97 bpm), obesity, prediabetes, and anemia place the patient at moderate‑to‑high 10‑year ASCVD risk. Renal risk: chronic NSAID use, hypertension, and anemia raise concern for early chronic kidney disease; eGFR is missing. Metabolic risk: obesity and prediabetes suggest metabolic syndrome; lipid panel and fasting glucose are absent. Musculoskeletal risk: knee osteoarthritis with chronic NSAID use. Hematologic risk: anemia of unclear etiology. Social risk: unstable housing may impede chronic disease management. Charlson comorbidity index is 1, clinical complexity is moderate.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value is missing; obesity is documented but quantitative BMI not available.
Renal function (eGFR) not recorded; important given hypertension, NSAID use, and anemia.
Lipid panel results are absent; needed for ASCVD risk calculation and statin decision.
LDL cholesterol missing; same as above.
Smoking history not documented; a key cardiovascular risk factor.
Laboratory data to characterize anemia are not present.

clinical_impression: A 60‑year‑old man with a cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors—stage 1 hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes—managed on dual antihypertensive therapy but lacking lipid and renal monitoring. Chronic knee osteoarthritis contributes to functional limitation and NSAID exposure, which may compromise blood pressure control and renal function. Anemia of unknown etiology and unstable housing further complicate care. Overall, the patient has moderate clinical complexity with several gaps in preventive care and risk‑factor assessment.
